ns2:course.label: Morality, Methods, and Medicine: Formal and Philosophical Approaches to Health in Society
ns2:course.description: Interdisciplinary, experiential Grand Challenge Learning course in Health & Wellness. Exploration of the ways methodological and moral principles interact to inform policy choices related to health and society; consideration of topics of ethical and public policy concern (e.g., abortion, animal experimentation, drug and trials, organ donation, vaccination, and provision of healthcare), with an emphasis on relevant formal, quantitative tools (e.g., probability, statistics, decision theory, modal logic, and graphical causal modeling).
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Restricted to students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing.
ns2:course.sectionDegreeAttributes: Grand Challenge-Health/Well, Hist&Philosoph Perspect, and Quant Reasoning II course.
ns2:course.classScheduleInformation: This course is intended for first and second year students.
